newsitem.title: USA: Unisys on track for savings of $600 mln.
newsitem.headline: Unisys on track for savings of $600 mln.

text.p: Unisys Corp said Wednesday it was on track toward achieving its goal of realizing annual cost savings of $600 million by year-end 1997 as a result of the restructuring announced in the 1995 fourth quarter.
Unisys said it has experienced lower-than-anticipated costs for workforce reductions associated with the restructuring.

As a result, it said it reversed certain 1995 restructuring reserves in the fourth quarter of 1996. This reversal was offset by charges of $84 million related to refocusing and discontinuing certain products and programs, it said.

"We have made good headway in 1996 under our new business structure," said James Unruh, chairman and chief executive officer. "We are working to build on that progress in the year ahead. Our business units are well positioned in their respective markets and focused on execution."
Unisys reported fourth quarter earnings per share of $0.15, after payment of preferred dividends, versus a loss of $0.16 a share a year earlier. Revenues slipped to $1.81 billion from $1.87 billion.
Unisys said its Global Customer Services unit continued good revenue growth, but Computer Systems revenues declined.
Unisys said Computer Systems made excellent progress in shipping previously delayed models of its new servers, but unit revenue declined as expected as it continued its product transition.
Information Services declined in the quarter. The unit had constrained growth in certain markets and continued to focus on improving profitability.
